finding.text: Fix 2 breaks the "fallback wrote first" guarantee for a real tab. `RecordWriter.post` now sends `client` on every verb (`core/Item/RecordWriter.js:56`), but the stamped lines it hands back as `rest` for the fallback carry no `client` (line 51). So the line the tab appends through `Append.js` is keyed `owner|ts`, while the late post is checked with `c:<client>|ts` (`Servex/agents/page_tools.js:149`). They never match, the late post writes a second line, and `doc/one-writer.md:231` ("the late post is answered `{already: true}`") is no longer true. `one-writer.test.mjs:103` still passes only because its late verb is posted without a `client`, which no real tab does any more. The fix: put `client` on the verb lines in `list` too, so the fallback line carries it, and add a case 3 variant that uses the real tab shape.

Fix 1 says "newline guard before **every** append" (fixes.md 1), and `core/doc/status.md`'s Phase 0 row now says "Done". But only `RecordWriter.append_once` has the guard. The two main append paths still append blind: the entry point's `write_line` (`Servex/agents/page_tools.js:183`, used by every `record_lines` and item-tool write) and the dev server's fallback (`Server/plugins/SocketServer/Append.js:131`). Either add the guard there with a test, or change the status row to say what is really covered.

Fix 5 changes the on-disk shape of every browser `List.add`: fields now sit under `data` instead of flat (`core/List/List.js:254-263`). Nobody checked the readers that read an `add` payload flat instead of through `hydrate()`. Examples: `ai/rail/rail.js:484` (`fold.content?.add?.text ?? …title`), `ai/cards/Activity.js:143` and `ai/AISession/SessionTimelineRows.js:97`. A card added to a page's content list from the browser would now show blank in those summaries. Do the census, then fix each reader or say why it can't receive these lines.

The F4 helper is a static on `Runtime` (`Server/plugins/SocketServer/Runtime.js:50`), and `rpc:write` is its only caller. fixes.md asks for "one crash-safe rewrite helper". Other rewriters still truncate in place: `Server/SessionConsolidate.mjs:110,132` uses plain `writeFileSync`. Consider moving the helper somewhere shared and listing its callers in status.md.

`safe_write` creates a `<file>.tmp-<pid>-<ms>` sibling inside the watched `public/` tree. LiveReload mutes only the real path (`Runtime.js:36`), so every save also queues a change for the tmp path, which is sent to every tab (`LiveReload.js:143-185`). That is probably harmless, because tabs ignore paths they didn't load, but it hasn't been checked.

Fix 2's second clause in fixes.md ("the item tool's own stamps repeat too (the flaky one-writer test)") is not addressed or mentioned. Fix 3 is marked "already built" with no test. The brief allows the skip, but status.md should link to the code that proves it (`ext/JSONL/live.js`, the `Socket.prototype.open` override).

Scope: this diff is step 1 (Phase 0) of the 8 steps only. Steps 2–8 (Ref/F7, Refs in `session.messages`, List-view hooks, `Sentence.at` + `Prompt.raw`, Prompt kind/items, session completion, the V1 compare) are not in it. Child task `s1` on `session.jsonl` is started but not completed. A fresh agent could continue from `plan.md` + `builder.md`.

Step 2 asked for a census of every caller that `add`s an already-owned item, switching the ones that meant a move to `move_to`. The diff has no census file, no switched caller, and nothing in `s2/` mentions one. The rule is now live (`core/List/List.js`, `add()`) and any such caller silently gets a Ref instead of the item. Write the census into `s2/` (even if it is "none found") and link it from `core/List/readme.md`.

The diff has no test that fails on the old behaviour at a real caller. `List.test.mjs` proves `add()` makes a Ref, but nothing shows the existing callers still work. Add a line to the census saying which suites were run after F7 (the builder's `core/` tests, `chat-messages.test.mjs`, the one-writer suite) and their counts.

`Chat.resurface` (`core/Session/Chat/Chat.js`) builds the Ref with `this.add({type:"Ref", path})`, so it never goes through the F7 branch. Its comment says F7 "would only make a Ref anyway", which is true only for live items. The two-line "Ref's add, then original's set" is not atomic: a crash between them leaves a Ref with no `resurfaced` mark. Say so in `core/Item/doc/ref.md`, or write the mark first.

`core/Session/Chat/doc/views-on-messages.md` and `doc/pseudo-properties.md` do not mention `resurfaced`. dictation-v3 owns the views and needs to know the mark exists and what it means ("dim the original"). Add a line to `views-on-messages.md` and send them a short note.

`foreign_ref` in `List.js` takes `dest.owner ?? dest` for the root. An unowned list that is not yet attached would give the wrong root and wrongly treat a cross-file item as same-file. Worth a test for a detached list.
`add()` now returns the Ref, not the item. Callers that chain on the return value (`list.add(x).set(...)`) would now edit the Ref. The census in finding 1 should check for this too.
The `Chat.test.mjs` pass line says "15 checks", but the diff shows 13 asserts plus the earlier 7. Count it with the runner rather than by hand (Law 7).

A fresh agent can continue from `builder.md` and `plan.md`, which are clear. `s2/` holds only `past-work.md` and `session.jsonl`, with no summary of what step 2 decided. Step 3 would have to read the diff to learn that `add()` answers the Ref and that `Chat.js` imports `Ref.js`.

Requirements met for this step: F7, a Ref hydrating in `session.messages` and resurface all exist, each with a test. The `List` and `Chat` readmes and `ref.md` are updated. The "Next" list in the Chat readme is accurate.

The owner's brief (requirements.md step 2, "F7: adding an item that already has a parent makes a Ref, never a move or a copy") is not met: `core/List/List.js` `add()` still moves, and only the new explicit `ref(x)` makes a Ref. The deviation is reasoned (CLAUDE.md "ask before" a core API's meaning) and recorded in plan.md decision 2, but nothing is queued as the follow-up, so the owner's F7 stays unbuilt. File a task (e.g. a new child of session.jsonl) to flip `add()` once the owner agrees, citing the census in plan.md.

Stale text now contradicts the decision. plan.md line 29 (step 2 list: "`List.add` makes a Ref") and builder.md step 2 ("`List.add(item)` ... adds `new Ref`") still describe the original F7. A fresh agent reading the step list would build the wrong thing; reword both to `list.ref()`.

`s2/` holds only `past-work.md` and `session.jsonl`, with no summary of what step 2 decided and built, and session.jsonl shows no `complete` line for task `s2`. Record the outcome (what landed, test counts, the `add()` vs `ref()` call) so step 3 can start from the folder alone.

`List.ref` (`core/List/List.js` ~line 317) has no covered edge cases: `x.root()` when `x` is unattached or its root has no `store.url` yields `{type:"Ref", url: undefined, path: ...}` with a meaningless path. Throw or document that `ref` needs an owned, attached item, and add a test for it.

Only steps 1 and 2 are in this diff; steps 3–8 (Refs written by Servex, List view hooks, `Prompt.raw`, Prompt kind/items, completion, V1 compare) are not built, and the Chat readme "Next" list correctly marks step 3 as open. The review verdict covers step 2 only.

`Chat.resurface` (`core/Session/Chat/Chat.js`) relies on two synchronous calls landing in one Store flush; this is stated in a comment and tested for state (`Chat.test.mjs`), but not for the single-write claim.

Requirement 1 (tests exist and run) is met for step 2: `List.test.mjs` and `Chat.test.mjs` extended (Chat reports 17 checks, F7 same-file and cross-file cases). Docs updated and indexed: `core/List/readme.md`, `core/Session/Chat/readme.md`, `core/Item/doc/ref.md`, `doc/views-on-messages.md` (`resurfaced` field).

Child sessions of a NESTED session get no Ref (Requirements 3; plan.md decision 3, "Refs for every session record"). `SessionRecord.is_chat_ref_target` also requires `is_session_dir`, a folder directly under a day, so `chat-model/session.jsonl` itself fails it. Its own spawn line (session.jsonl line 66, `minion-minion-chat-model-s3`, `"type":"Session"`) would get no Ref. But a `tasks.add` on the same file does get one, because page_tools checks `kind === "Session"`. Use one test for both writers (basename `session.jsonl` is enough to exclude a task's `task.jsonl`), and add a check with a session nested below a day-level session.

`core/Session/Chat/readme.md` line 56 says a spawned child session "gets the same Ref wherever `SessionRecord.add_ref` writes onto the session's own `session.jsonl`". It does not say that nested sessions are excluded, so the readme overstates what the code does (Law 9). Fix it together with finding 1.

The merge brings stale index lines: `public/framework/ai/sessions/files.jsonl` gains 11 `"gone":true` lines (`transcripts/`, `week.json`, `index.jsonl`, `sessions.json`, `spend-tree.json`, …). These files are gitignored and still exist in the main tree (checked with `ls`). The worktree's indexer wrote "gone" only because the worktree lacks them. After the merge, the index says that live files were deleted. Drop these lines from the merge, or have the indexer skip gitignored paths when it runs in a worktree.

The folder-making branch (`tasks.add` that makes its own task folder, then `record_new_folder`, then a Ref with `url: h.path`) has no test. The new checks cover the inline subtask (`path: tasks.<id>`) and `add_ref` only.
`ChatWriter.ref_line` always stamps `by: "servex"`, even when the writer is the `SessionRecord --links` sweep or `ChildLinks`. Passing the real writer would keep the record honest.

The shot page (`chat-model/builder/`) is not something this diff renders: the diff only appends a `{"file"}` line to it. At 1920 its task block has zero height (layout.json `ai-task` h 0), so only the title and "Files · 1" show and the page is 88% empty. At 400 the same block shows its tabs and report. This bug was already there before this diff and should be filed separately. The console also logs one 404 at each width.

Step 4 is only half done. The brief asks for a List view so that "any view just renders the list", and plan.md step 4 says "`ChatList` becomes 'render the list'". But `ext/Chat/list/ChatList.js:33-53` keeps its own keyed loop (`els` Map, `dirty` Set, `prev.after(el)`) and now has a second copy of the Ref → RefView branch. That makes two keyed reconcilers and two Ref branches (Law 6). Either draw `session.messages` through `DefaultView.reconcile()`, giving ChatList a `child()`-style hook that builds the bubble, or say in plan.md why ChatList stays separate.

`core/List/readme.md` (the new `List.View = DefaultView` bullet) says "ext/Chat/list draws `session.messages` through the same `DefaultView.reconcile()`". That is false: ChatList has its own `draw()` loop and never imports DefaultView (Law 9). Fix this together with finding 1, or reword it.

`List.View` is set only as a side effect of importing `ux/Content/Object/DefaultView.js` (DefaultView.js, end of file). On a page that never imports it, `list.render()` still returns `undefined` (`core/List/List.js:420`). The List readme says so, but nothing on the List page shows which pages get a view.

`ChatList.js:48` builds `new RefView({ ref: m, where: false })` without `capture: false`. If `draw()` ever runs inside a capturing render, the row lands in the captor first. That is the trap `ux/Content/Object/readme.md` warns about, and `DefaultView.reconcile()` passes `capture: false` for the same reason.

`list-view.test.mjs:4` imports `file:///C:/Code/lew42/monorepo/Server/Browser.mjs`, so from a worktree it runs the main tree's Browser. Its fallback base is `http://chat-model.localhost` (line 6), which goes stale once the worktree is gone; `TestRunner` passes `SITE_URL`, so it does run (results.jsonl: ok, 5655 ms, 05:55:59). Siblings in `ext/Chat/` use the same hard-coded path; `core/Task/TasksPage.test.mjs` shows the relative form.

`ext/Chat/list/fixture/session.jsonl` was regenerated (all 29 lines rewritten with new ids and times), but it still holds no Ref. So the demo at /framework/ext/Chat/list/ never shows the new `.chatlist-msg.is-ref` row that this step added. Add a `tasks.add` (or a Ref line) to the fixture writer so the demo shows the change.

Index churn: `public/framework/ai/files.jsonl`, `public/framework/files.jsonl` and the v2/v3 fixture `files.jsonl` gain pairs of add-then-`gone` lines for temporary test folders (`process-test-*`, `prompt-tasks-test-*`). They are harmless, but they are noise that a test cleanup should not write into the index.
The shots (400 and 1920) are of `chat-model/builder/`, which this diff does not render. No shot shows the List view or ChatList, so the browser test is the only visual proof of this step.
